topic: Your Visa Appointment Moved. What Happens to Your Flight Reservation?
metaTitle: Visa Appointment Moved? Your Flight Reservation Explained
metaDescription: Your visa appointment moved and the flight reservation is about to lapse. What expiry does to the booking reference, and how to time the new validity window.
excerpt: Appointments get rescheduled, and the flight reservation bought for the original date quietly expires. This guide explains what happens when a reservation lapses, why an unverifiable document in a submitted file is worse than a missing one, and how to pick the 2, 7 or 14 day window against an appointment date rather than a trip.
quickAnswer: Your reservation expires on its own clock, so the seat releases and the booking reference stops verifying, whether or not your appointment moved. Time the validity window to the appointment date, not the trip. We reissue with new dates free of charge when an appointment is rescheduled, and our tiers run AED 49 for 2 days, AED 69 for 7 days and AED 79 for 14 days.
content:
It expires on its own clock, and your new appointment date has nothing to do with it. A reservation holds a seat for a fixed window, and once that window closes the seat releases and the booking reference stops returning a result in the airline systems a consulate checks. Here is what that means for a file you are about to submit, and how to time the replacement properly.

What actually happens when a flight reservation expires?

Two things happen, and the second one is the problem. The held seat goes back into the airline's inventory, which nobody outside the airline notices or cares about. Then the record itself stops behaving like a live booking.

A flight reservation is a real record in a global distribution system, with a booking reference against your name, your route and your dates. While it is live, anyone with that reference can look it up in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport and see a confirmed itinerary. That lookup is the whole point of the document.

When the reservation lapses, the same lookup returns nothing, or returns a cancelled record. The PDF in your file still looks perfectly normal. It has the airline logo, the flight numbers, the times and a booking reference. It just no longer corresponds to anything.

That gap between how the document looks and what it does is exactly why this catches people out. You have no way of knowing from the paper itself that it has gone stale.

At a glance: reservations, appointments and timing

What should I do the moment my appointment moves?

Work through this in order. It takes about ten minutes and it saves the file.

  • Confirm the new appointment date in writing. The email or SMS from the visa centre, not the date you think you selected.
  • Check the validity window on your current reservation. It is the date the booking is held until, which is not the same as the departure date printed on it.
  • Work out whether the window still covers the new date. If the appointment lands after the hold expires, the document is already dead for your purposes.
  • Ask for a reissue rather than buying again. When an appointment has been rescheduled we issue new dates at no charge, so tell us the new date and the file reference.
  • Replace every copy. The printed one in your folder, the PDF on your phone and anything you have already uploaded to an online portal.
  • Re-check your other dated documents. Hotel reservations and insurance cover dates drift out of line with the flight dates just as easily.

Why is an expired reservation worse than having none at all?

Because of what the officer concludes when the lookup fails. A missing document is an incomplete file, and an incomplete file usually gets flagged at the counter or comes back with a request for more. Annoying, recoverable.

A document that cannot be verified is a different category. The officer is not sitting there thinking about validity windows and appointment reschedules. They typed a reference into a system, the system returned nothing, and now there is a question mark over the paperwork rather than over a date.

That question mark is hard to argue with after the fact, because you are explaining a timing accident to somebody who already formed an impression. Consistency across the file is one of the quiet things decisions turn on, and a reservation that does not match anything live reads as an inconsistency.

The practical rule is simple. Never submit a document you have not checked since the last time your dates changed. If you cannot confirm it is still live, replace it, and if you cannot replace it in time, it is better to explain a missing item than to hand over one that fails a check.

How do I choose between 2, 7 and 14 days when the date is uncertain?

Time the window against the appointment, not against the trip. This is the single mistake that produces most of these situations. People buy validity to cover their holiday, when what the validity has to cover is the day somebody opens the file.

So the question is not how long you are travelling. It is how much slack there is between now and the moment your documents get looked at, and how confident you are in that date.

Which validity tier suits which appointment scenario
TierPrice per travellerWhen it fits
2 daysAED 49The appointment is confirmed, it is within the next day or two, and you are walking the file in yourself. Also the right choice for a check-in desk or a border crossing, where the document is used once and then done with
7 daysAED 69The appointment is confirmed but a few days out, or the centre takes documents on one date and reviews them later in the week. The usual sensible default
14 daysAED 79The date is not settled, you are on a waiting list for an earlier slot, the centre has already moved you once, or you are submitting for a family and the slots are spread across different days

The gap between the cheapest and the longest tier is AED 30. Weigh that against redoing a submission, and the 14 day window is easy to justify whenever the date is genuinely in play.

One thing worth saying plainly: the tier buys validity, not route. A one way and a return cost the same, so there is nothing to gain by simplifying your itinerary to save money. Pick the window, then build the itinerary that matches what you are actually claiming you will do.

What if the visa centre moved the appointment, not me?

It happens more than people expect, and you have very little control over it. Appointment capacity is set by the government the centre works for rather than by the centre itself, and VFS Global states that slots are allocated on the directives of its client governments on a first come first served basis. When a consulate changes its allocation, dates move.

Rescheduling is handled through the country specific website for your application, and the process is not identical everywhere. Some routes let you move a booking online with your reference number. Others treat a missed appointment as a fresh start, with a waiting period before you can book again and a new fee.

US appointments have their own wrinkle. The official US visa appointment service caps how many times an applicant may reschedule, and the cap is set per consular post rather than globally, so check the page for the post you are applying at before you move anything. Running out of reschedules is a worse problem than an expired document.

Whichever way the date moved, our side of it is the same. Send us the new appointment date and we reissue with matching dates free of charge. Filing the application, booking your slot and moving it are not things we do, so go to the centre for the appointment and come to us for the paperwork.

Why do applications like this get refused?

Rarely because of the reservation alone. Decisions turn on funds, on ties to where you live, and on whether the story the file tells hangs together. A flight reservation is one thread in that, and no document on its own decides the outcome.

Where the reservation does real damage is in these specific ways:

  • It cannot be verified. The reference is dead, so the officer cannot confirm any travel arrangement exists.
  • The dates contradict the rest of the file. A reservation showing departure on a date your hotel booking and your leave letter disagree with.
  • The travel dates sit outside the permitted lodging window. For Schengen, an application has to be lodged no earlier than six months before the journey and at least 15 days before it, so an itinerary that no longer fits that frame raises an obvious question.
  • The passenger name does not match the passport. Trivial to fix before submission, impossible after.

Worth being clear about what the document is, because nervous applicants often assume the worst. A reservation of ours is a genuine booking made in a real airline system, not a mock-up. The fare simply has not been paid, which is precisely why it is appropriate for a file that is asking for evidence of travel arrangements rather than proof of a purchase. The EU Visa Code frames the Schengen requirement in terms of supporting documents about the journey, not a ticket you have already bought.

What do your reissue and refund policies actually cover?

Two separate things, and it is worth knowing where the line sits.

Reissue. If your appointment is rescheduled, we issue a reservation with new dates free of charge. Email the new date to info@thedummyticket.ae and it comes back in 10 to 15 minutes, the same as a new booking, around the clock.

Refund. There is one case, and only one. If you receive a refusal letter that says the reservation had expired or could not be verified, you get a full refund. That is the failure that is ours to own.

What is not covered: a change of plans, and a refusal on any other ground. If you decide not to travel, or the application is refused over funds, ties, history or anything else in the file, the refund does not apply. We would rather write that down than let you find it out later.

On verification, one honest caveat. The booking reference can be checked in Amadeus, Sabre and Travelport, which is where a consulate or an airline actually looks. Some airline websites will show an unpaid hold under Manage Booking and many will not, so treat the airline site as a bonus rather than the test.

What is the simplest way to avoid this entirely?

Book the reservation after the appointment is confirmed, not before, and pick the window from the appointment date. If you are booking ahead of a slot you do not have yet, take the 14 day tier and accept the AED 79.

Then set yourself a reminder for two days before the window closes. If the appointment has moved by then, you ask for a reissue with time to spare instead of discovering the problem in the queue. A reservation from The Dummy Ticket AE lands in your inbox in 10 to 15 minutes at any hour, so the replacement is never the slow part.

If you are unsure which window covers your situation, the FAQ page goes through validity, verification and reissues in more detail, or you can book a reservation from AED 49 and set the dates around the appointment you have in hand.

faqs.question: Does my flight reservation move automatically when my visa appointment is rescheduled?
faqs.answer: No. The reservation holds its original dates and expires on its own schedule, with no link to the visa centre. You have to ask for a reissue. When an appointment has been rescheduled we issue new dates free of charge, delivered in 10 to 15 minutes.

faqs.question: Can a visa officer tell that my flight reservation has expired?
faqs.answer: Yes. The PDF looks unchanged, but the booking reference no longer returns a live record in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport. The officer sees a lookup that fails, which reads as a document that cannot be verified rather than a date that slipped.

faqs.question: Should I buy the 2, 7 or 14 day reservation if my appointment date is not confirmed?
faqs.answer: Take the 14 day window at AED 79. The tier buys validity, not route, and the gap from the cheapest option is AED 30. Once a date is confirmed and close, the 7 day tier at AED 69 covers most submissions comfortably.

faqs.question: Do you refund if my visa is refused?
faqs.answer: Only in one case: a refusal letter stating the reservation had expired or could not be verified earns a full refund. A refusal on any other ground, such as funds or ties, is not covered, and neither is a change of plans on your side.

faqs.question: Can you reschedule my visa appointment for me?
faqs.answer: No. Appointments are booked and moved through the visa centre or consular website for your application, and slots are allocated on government directives. We sell the documents that go into a file, so send us the new date and we reissue to match.
